the r2 amendment's diagnosis of the vendored krawczyk operator is factually incorrect. It states (lines 96-98) that k_image (num/krawczyk.rs:162) IS the correct full-matrix Krawczyk, 'd[r][c] = delta - y[r][c]*j[r][c]', and is 'NOT limited to diagonal systems'. But d[r][c] = delta - y[r][c]*j[r][c] uses the SAME column index c on both Y and J: it is the ENTRYWISE (diagonal-preconditioner) contraction, not the matrix product (I - Y*J)_rc = delta_rc - sum_k y[r][k]*j[k][c]. It contracts only for systems whose interval Jacobian is effectively diagonal.

consequence: the 2x2 z-slab probe cannot certify ANY crossing of the transversal witness, contradicting the amendment's expectation. Re-derived determinant: J = [[2x, 2y], [2(x-cx), 2(y-cy)]], det = 4(y*cx - x*cy) = 12y for cx=3,cy=0 (nonsingular off the singular locus, as the packet states). But the entrywise (I - Y∘J) at any crossing (x,y) of the curve has row-1 |d|-sum = (x-3)^2/(3y) + |1 - x/3| >= 4/3 + 2/3 > 1 (x in [1/6,1], |y| <= 1 on the cylinder), so K ⊂ strict interior(Q) is unreachable on ANY axis-aligned box regardless of position, shape, or budget.

control measurement: the krawczyk module's OWN coupled 2x2 linear witness (Lin2, full-matrix preconditioner) certifies one-shot on a small box, but only because its entrywise (I - Y∘J) row sums are 0.4 < 1. This isolates the operator's behavior: it certifies iff (I - Y∘J) is small, i.e. only near-diagonal systems. The slab system at the crossing has row sums ~1.12 and ~3.24, so krawczyk returns NumericallyUnresolved even on a 0.02-wide box centered on the exact crossing (f residuals ~1e-16).
